final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with concrete enforcement: 75% RVC with 18-month phase-in from entry into force, $8M trilateral labor-monitor commission with quarterly audits and automatic 25% tariff snapback at 10% wage breach, Chapter 19 carved out for labor/environment disputes only (commodity dumping excluded), and dairy bilateral with Canada (20k MT fluid milk, 35k MT cheese TRQs). USTR committed to deliver complete trilateral text to Congress by Friday. Unresolved: per-facility compliance cost allocation for suppliers.
minority_objections: Supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly warned that ambiguous per-facility compliance costs would trigger immediate dual-sourcing to Mexico and Asia, undermining the integrated North American base the deal aims to protect
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada drew hard red line requiring mechanism for labor/environment; USTR initially refused any Chapter 19, then compromised by carving out commodity dumping
Dairy market access: Canada required bilateral carve-out with concrete TRQ numbers before signing; USTR initially resisted pre-locking outcomes
Labor enforcement specificity: Congress, labor, and industry demanded binding dollar amounts and audit frequencies in Friday text, not commission-determined frameworks
key_concessions: USTR accepted Chapter 19 mechanism for labor and environmental disputes (commodity dumping excluded)
USTR agreed to 18-month RVC phase-in from entry into force (not ratification)
Canada accepted dairy bilateral outside trilateral text with specific TRQ volumes (20k MT fluid milk, 35k MT cheese)
All parties accepted $8M trilateral-funded labor commission with automatic snapback (no dispute delay)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 mechanism for labor/environment disputes must survive in final text
Canada: Dairy TRQ numbers and bilateral signature timeline locked before Parliament vote
Congress: Complete trilateral text with all enforcement specifics by Friday, no post-ratification rewrites
Labor: Binding enforcement language with hard dollar amounts and automatic snapback in Congressional text
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Per-facility compliance cost allocation left unresolved despite repeated warnings from auto, labor, dairy, and supply-chain reps that ambiguity would trigger immediate dual-sourcing decisions
Automatic 25% tariff snapback mechanism may create political backlash in Mexico or compliance gaming, but no one tested Mexican acceptance
Compressed timeline (dairy signature Wednesday, complete text Friday, Congressional vote imminent) leaves no buffer for drafting errors or last-minute objections
downstream_risk_variables: Mexican political acceptance of automatic snapback with no dispute window
Canada Parliament ratification timeline vs. U.S. Congress vote sequencing
Actual drafting quality of Chapter 19 carve-out language (promised tonight, unvetted)
Commission audit capacity to execute quarterly facility inspections across three countries on $8M budget
uncertainty_notes: Per-facility compliance costs unresolved; Chapter 19 carve-out language promised tonight but not yet drafted or confirmed; dairy bilateral signature Wednesday depends on ag teams finalizing TRQ memo by 4:30 PM today; no confirmation that $8M budget can operationally support quarterly audits across North American auto supply chain; Mexican acceptance of automatic snapback not tested in room.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and labor-value-content floor drove the entire negotiation structure; 18-month phase-in compromise was the key concession that unlocked Canada's acceptance and industry support
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: $8M budget, quarterly audits, and automatic 25% snapback were the specific enforcement mechanisms Congress demanded and USTR locked into Friday text to secure ratification
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada required dairy bilateral with concrete TRQ numbers (20k/35k MT) and Wednesday signature as condition for joining package; USTR had to lock numbers by 4:30 PM today
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'if you kill it outright, Canada doesn't sign — full stop'; Chapter 19 carve-out for labor/environment was the compromise that enabled Canada's signature
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Sunset clause never mentioned; no discussion of review mechanisms or agreement duration
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress demanded complete trilateral text by Friday with all enforcement specifics locked, stating 'this deal dies in committee' if details slip post-vote; drove USTR's concrete commitments
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly raised per-facility compliance costs and dual-sourcing risk, but the room did not resolve cost allocation — acknowledged but not decisive
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico framed package as 'done deal' and stated 'we need Canada at the table accepting these terms, not renegotiating them'; U.S.-Mexico bilateral forming first was explicit leverage
